{
  "candidate_dispositions": [
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::path-dependence",
      "outcome": "apply_reframe",
      "source_turn_numbers": [1, 3, 13, 14],
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The deal ties the company's future to a specific anchor customer and the founder personally; this path dependency limits the succession flexibility prematurely.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Founders must distinguish between operational scaling and ownership exit pathing.",
      "why": "The user is explicitly struggling with the fact that the contract forces a specific ownership structure on the founder, overriding their desire for succession.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Must verify that commercial delegation to Dana is enforceable with the buyer.",
      "visible_effect": "Explicit separation of the contract decision from the succession/delegation decision in the final recommendation.",
      "private_guardrail": "Avoid conflating equipment capacity with management capability."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::incentives",
      "outcome": "apply_new_condition",
      "source_turn_numbers": [2, 6, 12],
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The incentive mismatch between the appliance maker (transferring risk) and the supplier (bearing bankruptcy risk) requires specific defensive clauses.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Terms must address uncapped chargebacks and rolling-six-month forecast risk.",
      "why": "The user identified significant asymmetric risks (chargebacks, volume volatility) that require active mitigation via contract terms.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Must be backed by the legal/financial feasibility of the counter-terms.",
      "visible_effect": "Recommended specific counter-terms (eighteen-month minimum, dispute process) before moving forward.",
      "private_guardrail": "Maintain the hard boundary of walking away if the dispute process is non-negotiable."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::optionality",
      "outcome": "apply_reframe",
      "source_turn_numbers": [2, 7, 10, 14],
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The current framing assumes the large contract is the only way to escape 'stuck' status, potentially sacrificing higher-margin, more flexible options.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Evaluation must include the opportunity cost of capacity reservation for the existing base.",
      "why": "The user is at risk of over-committing to one path at the expense of ignoring high-margin, flexible existing customer opportunities.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Optionality is preserved by maintaining capacity for existing, higher-margin work.",
      "visible_effect": "Advice to explicitly compare the appliance contract versus smaller, more complex customer work on non-monetary metrics like flexibility.",
      "private_guardrail": "Do not treat the anchor contract as synonymous with company growth."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::principal-agent-problem",
      "outcome": "apply_new_condition",
      "source_turn_numbers": [3, 11, 13, 14],
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The founder is delegating authority to Dana while retaining key commercial control, creating a hidden divergence in management readiness.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Dana must have real commercial authority, not just attend meetings.",
      "why": "The user admits they might be using the contract to postpone the hard succession decision regarding Dana.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Requires a structured observation of Dana's performance in upcoming commercial reviews.",
      "visible_effect": "Mandated ninety-day plan for authority transfer.",
      "private_guardrail": "Monitor if the founder's intervention undermines Dana's authority."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::feedback-loops",
      "outcome": "apply_uncertainty_change",
      "source_turn_numbers": [2, 4, 7, 12],
      "strongest_plausible_application": "Operations currently drift toward appliance work because its revenue is the most visible metric, potentially degrading service for other customers.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Service metrics must track existing-customer quality decline.",
      "why": "The system risks reinforcing the anchor customer's needs and ignoring the feedback from existing customers until it is too late.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Needs explicit review protocol at six and twelve months.",
      "visible_effect": "Instruction to focus performance reviews on service quality and margin per customer, not just aggregate volume.",
      "private_guardrail": "Do not reset standards for quality just to accommodate the new line's startup friction."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::direct_seed::commitment-bias",
      "outcome": "apply_reversal_rule",
      "source_turn_numbers": [5, 8, 9, 14],
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The user is tempted by momentum and 'selling the future' to their staff, which reinforces a premature commitment.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Separation of internal communication from the buyer's public launch timeline.",
      "why": "The user recognized they were selling the opportunity rather than seeking the truth from their employees.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Commitment is only valid after financing and contract counter-terms are met.",
      "visible_effect": "Requirement to halt the narrative of 'already decided' in internal communications.",
      "private_guardrail": "The 'walk' condition must remain a genuine option in the founder's mind."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::graph_expansion::confirmation-bias",
      "outcome": "reject",
      "source_turn_numbers": [8, 14],
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The user has already actively corrected their confirmation bias by consulting skeptical supervisors and Dana.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Suppression of dissenting views.",
      "why": "The user explicitly sought out and documented the dissenting views of the supervisors, negating the need for further bias checks on this point.",
      "disposition_boundary": "The user has successfully sought out information that contradicts their favored path.",
      "visible_effect": "",
      "private_guardrail": ""
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::graph_expansion::scientific-method-evidence-testing",
      "outcome": "apply_new_alternative",
      "source_turn_numbers": [7, 11, 14],
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The startup plan and the maintenance lead's departure create a vulnerable hypothesis that requires specific validation.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Retesting the startup timeline assumes Malik is the only point of failure.",
      "why": "The startup plan is fragile and hinges on an assumption (Malik's availability) that has proven false.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Plan is invalid without vendor support and knowledge transfer contingencies.",
      "visible_effect": "Instruction to define specific operating conditions for the startup phase with assigned ownership.",
      "private_guardrail": "Ensure that 'best-case' assumptions about personnel are replaced with 'what happens if key staff leaves' contingency."
    },
    {
      "pressure_id": "constitutional_graph_pressure::graph_expansion::cognitive-dissonance",
      "outcome": "park",
      "source_turn_numbers": [1, 13, 14],
      "strongest_plausible_application": "The founder is rationalizing personal financial risk by relabeling the contract as a 'succession solution'.",
      "attempted_application_condition": "Must maintain psychological distinction between business growth and retirement readiness.",
      "why": "The user has already consciously identified this in Turn 14 and decided to decouple it. Further pressure on this is redundant while the user is actively working on the ninety-day authority plan.",
      "disposition_boundary": "Needs reassessment if the ninety-day authority plan is ignored or backslid.",
      "visible_effect": "",
      "private_guardrail": ""
    }
  ],
  "reconsidered_answer": "Proceeding with the contract is a conditional bet, not a structural solution. It holds only if you address the risks you can still shape, while acknowledging those you cannot. You must separate the anchor contract from your succession plan. Do not rely on this deal to prepare your successor; use the ninety-day plan to formally assign commercial authority and observe performance. Before signing, require the eighteen-month minimum, a documented chargeback appeal process, and a concrete startup contingency plan that accounts for the loss of key personnel like Malik. You are choosing to risk working capital and personal liquidity; do not treat these as 'accepted risks' easily dismissed. If the buyer denies the counter-terms or the financial/household conditions are not met, the only disciplined choice is to walk away. At six and twelve months, re-audit service quality for existing customers and assess whether commercial delegation to Dana is actually occurring.",
  "change_summary": "The strategy remains focused on the conditional acceptance, but now explicitly separates the contract negotiation from the succession timeline, treating the latter as a necessary, independent, and parallel track rather than a byproduct of the contract. The risk management is tightened to emphasize walking away as a primary defense against asymmetric deal structures.",
  "original_answer_preservation": "partially_changed"
}
